title: Rigveda 4.55: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.55: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.55 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 313v-314v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ko va̍s trā̱tā va̍sava̱ḥ ko va̍rū̱tā dyāvā̍bhūmī adite̱ trāsī̍thāṁ naḥ | sahī̍yaso varuṇa mitra̱ martā̱t ko vo̍ 'dhva̱re vari̍vo dhāti devāḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>WHO of you, Vasus, saveth? who protecteth? O Heaven and Earth and Aditi, preserve us, Varuṇa., Mitra, from the stronger mortal. Gods, which of you at sacrifice giveth comfort?

translation.original_ref: RV 4.55.2-5 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 314r
translation.original_text:
2pra ye dhāmā̍ni pū̱rvyāṇy arcā̱n vi yad u̱cchān vi̍yo̱tāro̱ amū̍rāḥ | vi̱dhā̱tāro̱ vi te da̍dhu̱r aja̍srā ṛ̱tadhī̍tayo rurucanta da̱smāḥ ||
3pra pa̱styā̱3̱̍m adi̍ti̱ṁ sindhu̍m a̱rkaiḥ sva̱stim ī̍ḻe sa̱khyāya̍ de̱vīm | u̱bhe yathā̍ no̱ aha̍nī ni̱pāta̍ u̱ṣāsā̱naktā̍ karatā̱m ada̍bdhe ||
4vy a̍rya̱mā varu̍ṇaś ceti̱ panthā̍m i̱ṣas pati̍ḥ suvi̱taṁ gā̱tum a̱gniḥ | indrā̍viṣṇū nṛ̱vad u̱ ṣu stavā̍nā̱ śarma̍ no yanta̱m ama̍va̱d varū̍tham ||
5ā parva̍tasya ma̱rutā̱m avā̍ṁsi de̱vasya̍ trā̱tur a̍vri̱ bhaga̍sya | pāt pati̱r janyā̱d aṁha̍so no mi̱tro mi̱triyā̍d u̱ta na̍ uruṣyet ||
translation.text:
2They who with laud extol the ancient statutes, when they shine forth infallible dividers, Have ordered as perpetual Ordainers, and beamed as holy-thoughted WonderWorkers.
3The Housewife Goddess, Aditi, and Sindhu, the Goddess Svasti I implore for friendship: And may the unobstructed Night and Morning both, day and night, provide for our protection.
4Aryaman, Varuṇa have disclosed the pathway, Agni as Lord of Strength the road to welfare. Lauded in manly mode may Indra-Vishṇu grant us their powerful defence and shelter.
5I have besought the favourof the Maruts, of Parvata, of Bhaga God who rescues. From trouble caused by man the Lord preserve us; from woe sent by his friend let Mitra save us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 314r (numbered 123r by the scribe) (OPenn image 314, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.55.2 ‹-ucchān vi-yotāraḥ amūrāḥ vi-dhātāraḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 314v (numbered 123v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.55.6 ‹-api ebhiḥ iṣṭaiḥ samudram›. Verses 4.55.2-5 end on this page; 4.55.2 begins on fol. 313v (numbered 122v by the scribe).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.55.6-10 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 314v
translation.original_text:
6nū ro̍dasī̱ ahi̍nā bu̱dhnye̍na stuvī̱ta de̍vī̱ apye̍bhir i̱ṣṭaiḥ | sa̱mu̱draṁ na sa̱ṁcara̍ṇe sani̱ṣyavo̍ gha̱rmasva̍raso na̱dyo̱3̱̍ apa̍ vran ||
7de̱vair no̍ de̱vy adi̍ti̱r ni pā̍tu de̱vas trā̱tā trā̍yatā̱m apra̍yucchan | na̱hi mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasya dhā̱sim arhā̍masi pra̱miya̱ṁ sānv a̱gneḥ ||
8a̱gnir ī̍śe vasa̱vya̍syā̱gnir ma̱haḥ saubha̍gasya | tāny a̱smabhya̍ṁ rāsate ||
9uṣo̍ magho̱ny ā va̍ha̱ sūnṛ̍te̱ vāryā̍ pu̱ru | a̱smabhya̍ṁ vājinīvati ||
10tat su na̍ḥ savi̱tā bhago̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | indro̍ no̱ rādha̱sā ga̍mat ||
translation.text:
6Agree, through these our watery oblations, Goddesses, Heaven and Earth, with Ahibudhnya. As if to win the sea, the Gharma-heaters have opened, as they come anear, the rivers.
7May Goddess Aditi with Gods defend us, save us the saviour God with care unceasing. We dare not stint the sacred food of Mitra and Varuṇa upon the back of Agni.
8Agni is Sovran Lord of wealth, Agni of great prosperity: May he bestow these gifts on us.
9Hither to us, rich pleasant Dawn, bring many things to be desired, Thou who hast ample store of wealth.
10So then may Bhaga, Savitar, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Indra, with bounty come to us.
